data.name: Ashank
data.gender_notes: Ashank is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the name Ashwin, meaning horse or the invincible. In Hindu mythology, Ashank is considered a descendant of the Ashwin twins, the divine physicians and horse-riding gods. It is believed that this name brings good fortune, courage, and strength. The name Ashank carries the meaning “Ashwin's descendant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashank usually hope their child will grow to embody ashwin's descendant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine protection and blessings from the Ashwin twins.
data.etymology: Ashank belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ashwin's descendant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashank total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ashish is widely used in the Indian subcontinent, especially in the Hindu, Jain, and Sikh communities. The use of personal names influences various aspects of our daily lives, and the name Ashish can elicit admiration and respect due to its strong cultural association.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ashish is derived from the Sanskrit word Ashishah, meaning "to make peaceful." It is also associated with the Aishvarya Ashtakam, a devotional hymn dedicated to Lord Krishna, which contains the invocation, "O Ashish Mukhacheen, may my mind ever remain intelligent and peaceful."
